title: Playing at the Kingley House in the Irish Channel
summary: Nervous about the Irish Channel's reputation, he plays 'It's a Long Way to Tipperary' and finds the crowd courteous.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Just like up at... When I played up at the Kingley House. I was... I heard so much about the Irish Channel, you understand? I never was in trouble in my life. So... I was kind of leery about going up there and playing. For fear that I'd get mixed up with some of them Irishmen up there. And... So uh... The fella that had the job. He says, Oh, you don't have Jake Steven. He said, You don't have to worry. Them people ain't gonna bother you. He says, All you gotta do is sit upon your... Sit upon the stand and... Intermission you can get down. So they had a piece. It's a long ways to Tipperary. You understand? Yeah. And uh... We was playing up there. And we played this long ways to Tipperary. A fella come up there to the stand. After the next piece we played. He says, Say young man. He says, I wouldn't mind if you'd play that in a long ways to Tipperary. Again, he says, I'll treat the whole gang easy. So I said, Well you don't have to treat the gang. I said, You don't have to treat me. But I said, If you want that to play it again, I'll... He says, We'll play it. Well that fella, I swear, Every time you'd play Tipperary, You wouldn't play two pieces, But he didn't come back. And he wanted you to play a long ways to Tipperary. So I told him, I says to him, I said, You must be a pure bread Irishman. I said, Damn it, you carry that Irish in your pocket, I believe. So, He says, Well I like that piece. I said, Well, I hope the other folks like it. He says, Well, you know Tipperary was a wonderful city. And he says, He says, I got stuck on the piece. Now we played Tipperary up there, man, To a fair you were. But I found those fellas up there, Entirely different from the way I thought they were. They all acted like gentlemen to us. I was afraid to go up there to play. Cause I never liked getting any kind of trouble.
